printing_evidence.directly_read: AP1 names Daily Missal with Vespers, Dom Gaspar Lefebvre, St Andrew Abbey and Lohmann and has no publication year. AP2 prints approvals of 21 March 1924 and 13 May 1925, plus All rights reserved. AP3 prints the letter of 13 May 1925 and visibly carries the physical JAN 20 27 accession stamp. William Busch is identified as censor; these pages do not identify him as translator.
printing_evidence.selected_leaf_evidence: AP1777–1779 are continuous ordinary printed folios 1737–1739. The Second and Third Mass headings explicitly prescribe the following Collects after general Anniversary/Daily referrals; these are therefore their own appointed orations. The three exact settings share regular typography, running heads and folios with the surrounding November 2 material. The Third Collect finishes before Secret and the later November 3 heading; no selected setting carries a separate later-insert label or lettered folio.
printing_evidence.bounded_inference: The approvals, physical accession mark and continuous selected settings support a bounded early, pre-1931 expression inference for these three settings. They do not prove an exact 1925 printing date. The existing edition record and filename are not used as independent proof of that year or of the exact new scope.
printing_evidence.strongest_contrary: Approvals date approval, not publication. A front-leaf accession stamp alone cannot exclude later insertion, replacement, rebinding or recomposition of other leaves. Continuous folios and matching setting strengthen but do not logically eliminate that possibility. The composite has lettered settings elsewhere. No whole-book authentication is claimed.
